en.title: Minimum Cost of Removing Two of the First Three Items
en.description:
Each time, choose any two of the first three elements of the current array and delete them; the cost of the operation is the larger of the two deleted numbers. If fewer than three elements remain, delete all the remaining elements at once, at a cost equal to their maximum. Find the minimum total cost to empty the array.

The standard input/output, the ranges added by this site, and the examples follow this problem's description; wherever the source's ranges are missing, they are explicitly marked as this site's additions.
en.input: The first line contains n (1≤n≤1000); the second line contains n positive integers, 1≤arr[i]≤10^6. The ranges are taken from the original problem's constraints.
en.explanation: After the first three items are processed, exactly one item remains. Use dynamic programming to record "value kept at the current front → minimum cost paid to reach this state". In each round, consider that value together with the next two items and enumerate which one stays; when fewer than three items remain at the end, settle them all at once as the statement specifies.
